title: Update the bundled libpcap headers to 1.10.6
description:
This doesn't have much if anything that affects how we use it.
We use the numbers directly instead of the DLT_ defines for
translating pcap linktype to WTAP encapsulations in libwiretap,
for example.

Ping #20013

notes.body:
From the original commit message for these headers:

    Other files (including pcap.h) have the provision but mentioning the
    Computer Systems Engineering Group at LBL; that might still apply
    (hopefully it does not.) If it *is* a problem, then it's always been
    a problem, because we've always distributed packages including these
    headers.

Unfortunately, the LBL provision still remains; I made some effort to try to find out who at LBL could authorize the three-clausing of libpcap and tcpdump, but couldn't find anybody.

The files to which this commit adds the fourth clause are largely written by some Guy who just grabbed some other file, which happened not to mention LBL in the advertising clause, as a skeleton and added the structures, so it's not *really* from anything Berkeley-connected, but it is what it is. I guess I could relicense it under some random license such as [the Beerware License](https://spdx.org/licenses/Beerware.html), although I'm not a beer drinker, so....

In any case, either leave the advertising clause in or leave it out, I don't know how much it matters. (I *think* the idea was to have those as public headers for people writing packet sniffers, but tcpdump has its own versions of those headers so as not to require a version of libpcap that exports them, so....)
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
